title: Jeremiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:1, what does the LORD say despite Israel playing the harlot with many lovers?
questions.correctAnswer: Return again to me
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:1 states that although Israel has played the harlot with many lovers, the LORD says 'yet return again to me.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 3:2, where are the people told to lift up their eyes and look?
questions.correctAnswer: Unto the high places
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:2 commands to 'Lift up thine eyes unto the high places.'

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 3:3 says the showers and latter rain were withheld because of Israel's unashamed whoredoms.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:3 explains that the showers have been withheld and there was no latter rain because Israel had a 'whore's forehead' and refused to be ashamed.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:4 say the people should cry unto the LORD from this time?
options: My father, thou art the guide of my youth
questions.correctAnswer: My father, thou art the guide of my youth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:4 asks if they will not cry unto the LORD, saying, 'My father, thou art the guide of my youth.'

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 3:5 asks if the LORD will keep His anger forever and notes that Israel has done as much evil as possible.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:5 questions if the LORD will keep His anger forever, and it states that Israel has spoken and done evil things as much as they could.

questions.question: During whose reign did the LORD say He observed backsliding Israel, according to Jeremiah 3:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah the king
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:6 states that the LORD spoke during the days of Josiah the king.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 3:7 says Israel turned back to the LORD immediately after being called.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:7 states Israel was called to turn to the LORD but she returned not.

questions.question: What did the LORD give Israel because of her backslidings, according to Jeremiah 3:8?
questions.correctAnswer: A bill of divorce
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:8 states that due to Israel's adultery, the LORD gave her a bill of divorce.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:9, what did Israel commit adultery with?
questions.correctAnswer: Stones and stocks
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:9 says Israel committed adultery with stones and with stocks.

questions.question: Which sister is described as treacherous in Jeremiah 3:7 and 3:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: Both Jeremiah 3:7 and 3:8 refer to Judah as the treacherous sister who also played the harlot.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 3:1, what analogy is used to describe the pollution caused by returning to a divorced wife who married another man?
options: The land will be greatly polluted
The fields will yield no fruit
questions.correctAnswer: The land will be greatly polluted
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:1 uses the analogy, 'shall not that land be greatly polluted?' to describe the uncleanliness of returning to a divorced wife who has married someone else.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 3:2 says Israel has not polluted the land with whoredoms and wickedness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:2 explicitly states that Israel 'hast polluted the land with thy whoredoms and with thy wickedness.'

questions.question: What example is given in Jeremiah 3:2 to describe how Israel has sat for the idols?
options: As the Arabian in the wilderness
As the lion in the forest
As the eagle on the mountain
As the sheep in the fold
questions.correctAnswer: As the Arabian in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:2 says Israel 'hast sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness.'

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:5, what type of things has Israel done?
options: Good things with all thy heart
questions.correctAnswer: Evil things as thou couldest
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:5 says Israel has 'spoken and done evil things as thou couldest.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 3:6, where had backsliding Israel gone to play the harlot?
options: Upon every high mountain and under every green tree
Only in the valley of the shadow
questions.correctAnswer: Upon every high mountain and under every green tree
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:6 states Israel went 'upon every high mountain and under every green tree' to play the harlot.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:10, how has Judah responded to the LORD despite her treachery?
options: She has turned with her whole heart
She has completely ignored the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: She has turned feignedly
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:10 states that Judah has not turned to the LORD with her whole heart, but only feignedly, showing insincere repentance. This reflects a superficial return rather than genuine obedience, as confirmed by the contrast with Israel's actions in verse 11.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about backsliding Israel compared to treacherous Judah in Jeremiah 3:11?
options: Israel has justified herself less than Judah
Israel has justified herself more than Judah
Judah is more righteous than Israel
Both Israel and Judah have fully repented
questions.correctAnswer: Israel has justified herself more than Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:11 clearly states that backsliding Israel has justified herself more than treacherous Judah, indicating Israel’s greater self-righteousness or excuse-making compared to Judah's behavior, highlighting the spiritual condition of both.

questions.question: What promise does Jeremiah 3:12 give to backsliding Israel if she returns?
options: The LORD will cause His anger to fall upon them
The LORD will be merciful and not keep anger forever
The LORD will destroy their enemies
The LORD will give them earthly riches
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will be merciful and not keep anger forever
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:12 promises that if Israel returns, the LORD will show mercy and will not keep His anger forever, offering hope and restoration to repentant sinners, consistent with the call to acknowledge their sins in verse 13.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:13, what must Israel acknowledge to receive mercy?
options: They have obeyed the LORD fully
They have scattered their ways to strangers and disobeyed God
They have been faithful in worship
questions.correctAnswer: They have scattered their ways to strangers and disobeyed God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:13 instructs Israel to acknowledge their iniquity and transgressions, specifically how they scattered their ways to strangers and failed to obey God's voice. This confession is necessary for receiving the mercy described in verse 12.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 3:14 describe the LORD’s relationship to His people?
options: As a king ruling over subjects
As a husband married to His people
questions.correctAnswer: As a husband married to His people
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 3:14, the LORD says, 'for I am married unto you,' illustrating a covenantal, intimate relationship with His people, encouraging them to return as a loving spouse calls back a wayward partner, reinforcing the call to repentance.

questions.question: What will the LORD provide to His people according to Jeremiah 3:15?
options: Pastors according to His heart to feed them knowledge and understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Pastors according to His heart to feed them knowledge and understanding
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:15 promises that God will give pastors who align with His heart and will feed the people with knowledge and understanding, emphasizing spiritual guidance and growth as part of restoration.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:16, what will happen when the people are multiplied and increased in the land?
options: They will build many altars to the LORD
They will no longer mention or remember the ark of the covenant
They will travel to foreign lands
questions.correctAnswer: They will no longer mention or remember the ark of the covenant
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:16 states that in those days, when the people are increased, they will say no more 'The ark of the covenant of the LORD' and will no longer remember or visit it, indicating a new phase of worship not dependent on the physical ark.

questions.question: What will Jerusalem be called according to Jeremiah 3:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Throne of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:17 declares that Jerusalem will be called the throne of the LORD when all nations gather there in His name, signifying the central place of divine rule and worship.

questions.question: What unity is described in Jeremiah 3:18 for the days to come?
options: The house of Judah will dominate over Israel
The house of Israel will be scattered forever
The house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel and come together from the north
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel and come together from the north
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:18 describes a future time when Judah and Israel will unite and return from the north to the land given to their fathers, illustrating restoration and reconciliation of the divided kingdoms.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 3:19 express God’s desire for His people?
options: That they call Him Master and serve Him out of fear
That they call Him Father and not turn away from Him
questions.correctAnswer: That they call Him Father and not turn away from Him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:19 reveals God's longing for His people to call Him 'My father' and remain faithful, highlighting the personal and familial nature of the relationship He desires.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 3:20, how has Israel dealt with God, as a wife does with her husband?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:20 compares Israel's treatment of God to a wife treacherously departing from her husband, indicating betrayal and unfaithfulness, making 'True' the correct answer.

questions.question: What is heard on the high places according to Jeremiah 3:21?
options: Weeping and supplications of the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Weeping and supplications of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:21 describes a voice heard on the high places as weeping and supplications from Israel, indicating repentance and sorrow for their sins.

questions.question: What is the LORD's response to the backsliding children in Jeremiah 3:22?
options: He will heal their backslidings if they return
He will remove them from the land
questions.correctAnswer: He will heal their backslidings if they return
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:22 invites the backsliding children to return with the promise that the LORD will heal their backslidings, showing God's mercy and readiness to restore.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:23 say about hope for salvation from hills and mountains?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:23 states that hoping for salvation from hills and mountains is in vain, and that true salvation is found only in the LORD our God, making 'True' the correct answer.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 3:25 describe the feelings of the people because of their sin?
options: They lie down in shame and are covered with confusion
questions.correctAnswer: They lie down in shame and are covered with confusion
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:25 explains that the people lie down in shame and confusion because they have sinned against the LORD, showing the deep remorse and recognition of their disobedience.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:19, what does the LORD desire Israel to call Him?
questions.correctAnswer: My Father
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:19 states, 'Thou shalt call me, My father; and shalt not turn away from me,' indicating God's desire for a paternal, intimate relationship with Israel.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 3:20, what metaphor is used to describe Israel's relationship with the LORD?
options: A wife treacherously departing from her husband
questions.correctAnswer: A wife treacherously departing from her husband
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:20 says, 'Surely as a wife treacherously departeth from her husband, so have ye dealt treacherously with me,' using this metaphor to express Israel's unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What was heard upon the high places according to Jeremiah 3:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Weeping and supplications
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:21 describes a voice heard upon the high places as 'weeping and supplications of the children of Israel,' indicating sorrow and repentance.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do for the backsliding children in Jeremiah 3:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Heal their backslidings
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:22 states, 'Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings,' showing God's mercy and readiness to restore them.

questions.question: Jeremiah 3:23 states that salvation is truly found where?
questions.correctAnswer: In the LORD our God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:23 emphasizes, 'Truly in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel,' contrasting futile hope in hills and mountains with true salvation in God.

questions.question: What has shame devoured according to Jeremiah 3:24?
options: The labour of our fathers from our youth
questions.correctAnswer: The labour of our fathers from our youth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:24 says, 'For shame hath devoured the labour of our fathers from our youth,' indicating that shame has consumed the fruits of their ancestors' work.

questions.question: What is the confession made in Jeremiah 3:25 about Israel and their ancestors?
options: They have obeyed the LORD perfectly
They have sinned and not obeyed the voice of the LORD
They have worshiped only the true God
They have been faithful to the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: They have sinned and not obeyed the voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:25 confesses, 'we have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our fathers... and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD,' acknowledging continuous disobedience.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God as a Father calling His people to return, similar to Jeremiah 3:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 64:8
questions.explanation: Isaiah 64:8 says, 'But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter,' similarly portraying God as Father, echoing Jeremiah 3:19's theme.

questions.question: Jeremiah 3:22 includes a call to return and a promise. Which New Testament passage echoes the promise of healing for repentant sinners?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 John 1:9
questions.explanation: 1 John 1:9 promises forgiveness and cleansing from sin upon confession, paralleling Jeremiah 3:22's promise to heal backslidings upon return.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 3:20 where Israel is compared to a treacherous wife, illustrating the relationship between God and Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:20 uses a simile ('as a wife treacherously departeth from her husband') to vividly describe Israel's unfaithfulness, comparing two unlike things using 'as'.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'backsliding' in Jeremiah 3:22 (שׁוּב, shub) primarily means what?
questions.correctAnswer: To return or repent
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root שׁוּב (shub) means 'to turn back' or 'return,' often used in prophetic texts to denote repentance, as in Jeremiah 3:22's call to return.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 3:18, which two groups are said to walk together and come to the land given to their fathers?
options: The house of Israel and the house of Judah
The northern tribes and the southern tribes
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Israel and the house of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:18 states, 'the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel,' indicating a future reunification and return to their ancestral land.

questions.question: What is the promise concerning pastors in Jeremiah 3:15?
options: They will feed with knowledge and understanding
They will be kings and rulers
They will bring destruction to enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will feed with knowledge and understanding
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:15 promises, 'I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding,' emphasizing nurturing leadership.

questions.question: Which earlier Torah commandment is thematically connected to the call in Jeremiah 3:14 where the LORD says, 'I am married unto you'?
options: Exodus 20:5 - You shall have no other gods before me
Deuteronomy 7:3 - Do not intermarry with other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 20:5 - You shall have no other gods before me
questions.explanation: The marriage metaphor in Jeremiah 3:14 relates to covenant faithfulness, echoing Exodus 20:5's prohibition against idolatry as spiritual adultery.

questions.question: Jeremiah 3:17 prophesies about Jerusalem being called what in the future?
questions.correctAnswer: Throne of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:17 states, 'At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the LORD,' signifying its role as God's sovereign seat among the nations.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is prominently displayed in the LORD's invitation to Israel in Jeremiah 3:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:12 explicitly states, 'for I am merciful, saith the LORD, and I will not keep anger for ever,' highlighting God's attribute of mercy in calling backsliding Israel to repentance.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 3:5, what question is posed about God's anger towards Israel's evil?
options: Will God keep His anger forever?
questions.correctAnswer: Will God keep His anger forever?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:5 asks, 'Will he reserve his anger for ever? will he keep it to the end?' emphasizing the tension between God's justice and His willingness to forgive.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:14 reveal about the relationship between God and His people?
options: God is married to His people
questions.correctAnswer: God is married to His people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:14 states, 'for I am married unto you,' depicting the covenantal relationship between God and Israel as that of a husband and wife, symbolizing intimacy and commitment.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by God giving 'pastors according to mine heart' in Jeremiah 3:15?
options: Doctrine of Shepherding and Spiritual Leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Shepherding and Spiritual Leadership
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:15 promises God will provide pastors who will feed His people with knowledge and understanding, reflecting the doctrine that God appoints spiritual leaders to nurture His flock.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 3:18 contribute to the biblical narrative of restoration?
options: It foretells the reunion of Israel and Judah
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem
It describes the exile in Babylon
It documents the building of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It foretells the reunion of Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:18 speaks of 'the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel,' indicating a future restoration and unity between the divided kingdoms, fitting into the redemptive theme of reconciliation.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Jeremiah 3:20 and Jeremiah 3:22 provide about Israel's relationship with God?
options: Israel's treachery is met with God's call to repentance and healing
Israel's righteousness secures their eternal place
God abandons Israel due to their sins
Israel is condemned without hope of restoration
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's treachery is met with God's call to repentance and healing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:20 likens Israel's betrayal to a wife’s treachery, while 3:22 invites the 'backsliding children' to return so God may heal them, together illustrating both human sinfulness and divine mercy.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:9 mean when it says Israel 'committed adultery with stones and with stocks'?
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry involving inanimate objects
questions.explanation: The phrase in Jeremiah 3:9 symbolizes Israel's idolatry, worshipping lifeless idols ('stones and stocks'), which is figurative adultery against God, a key biblical theme (Exodus 20:3-5).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's anger in the Old Testament is unending and unforgiving. How does Jeremiah 3:12-13 refute this claim?
options: God declares He will not keep anger forever and calls for acknowledgment of sin
God promises immediate destruction without mercy
God changes His mind frequently without reason
questions.correctAnswer: God declares He will not keep anger forever and calls for acknowledgment of sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:12-13 teaches that God is merciful and will not maintain anger forever, inviting Israel to confess their transgressions, thus showing a just but gracious God contrary to the sceptics’ claim.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:16 imply about the significance of the Ark of the Covenant in future worship?
options: The Ark will no longer be remembered or needed
The Ark will be central to worship forever
The Ark will be destroyed in battle
The Ark will be hidden from Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Ark will no longer be remembered or needed
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:16 predicts a time when the Ark of the Covenant is no longer recalled or visited, implying a new mode of worship beyond the physical symbol, pointing toward a spiritualized relationship with God.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 3:17 describe the future role of Jerusalem in God's plan?
options: It will be called the throne of the LORD and a gathering place for all nations
It will be destroyed and forgotten
It will be the capital of a worldly empire
It will be a city of idol worship
questions.correctAnswer: It will be called the throne of the LORD and a gathering place for all nations
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states Jerusalem will be the LORD’s throne and a center where all nations gather in His name, revealing its eschatological importance in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:6 reveal about Israel's sin during Josiah's reign?
options: Israel committed harlotry on high mountains and under green trees
Israel built altars only in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Israel committed harlotry on high mountains and under green trees
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:6 describes Israel's idolatrous worship in elevated places and groves, showing persistent spiritual unfaithfulness during Josiah's time.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and confession is taught by Jeremiah 3:13?
options: Acknowledgment of iniquity is necessary for repentance
Sin can be ignored without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Acknowledgment of iniquity is necessary for repentance
questions.explanation: Verse 13 calls Israel to 'acknowledge thine iniquity,' teaching the biblical doctrine that genuine repentance requires confessing one's sins before God (1 John 1:9).

questions.question: What combined teaching about Israel's unfaithfulness and God's response is found in Jeremiah 3:7-8 and Jeremiah 3:10-11?
options: Israel and Judah both committed spiritual adultery, but God views Israel as more justified in her backsliding
Judah was faithful while Israel was not
God abandoned both Israel and Judah completely
Israel was faithful and Judah was rebellious
questions.correctAnswer: Israel and Judah both committed spiritual adultery, but God views Israel as more justified in her backsliding
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:7-8 describe Israel's and Judah's spiritual adultery; 3:10-11 reveals that Israel justified herself more than Judah, indicating God's nuanced judgment on their sinfulness.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 3:23 teach about the source of Israel's salvation?
options: Salvation is found only in the LORD our God, not in geographical features
Salvation comes from the hills and mountains
Salvation is found in foreign gods
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is found only in the LORD our God, not in geographical features
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states that hoping for salvation from hills and mountains is vain; true salvation is in the LORD, emphasizing God's exclusive role as Savior (Isaiah 45:22).

questions.question: What theological truth about divine guidance and youthful relationship is expressed in Jeremiah 3:4?
options: God is the guide of one's youth and a loving Father
God abandons the young in their rebellion
Youth does not need divine guidance
questions.correctAnswer: God is the guide of one's youth and a loving Father
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:4 invites Israel to cry to God as 'My father, thou art the guide of my youth,' expressing a personal and formative relationship with God as Father and guide.
